title: One more match
setting: A Saturday evening at home. Kenji, Yuki's little brother, is slumped on the sofa playing a football video game when Yuki comes in with some news.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenji, mata sono geemu shiteru no? kinou mo osoku made shiteta desho.
lines.ja: ケンジ、またそのゲームしてるの？昨日も遅くまでしてたでしょ。
lines.kana: けんじ、またそのげーむしてるの？きのうもおそくまでしてたでしょ。
lines.english: Kenji, playing that game again? You were on it till late last night too, weren't you?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. saikin, kono geemu ni metcha hamatteru n da.
lines.ja: うん。最近、このゲームにめっちゃハマってるんだ。
lines.kana: うん。さいきん、このげーむにめっちゃはまってるんだ。
lines.english: Yeah. I'm totally hooked on this game lately.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sakkaa no geemu ka. de, tsuyoi no?
lines.ja: サッカーのゲームか。で、強いの？
lines.kana: さっかーのげーむか。で、つよいの？
lines.english: A football game, huh. So, are you any good?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: uun. kyou no shiai, zenbu maketa.
lines.ja: ううん。今日の試合、全部負けた。
lines.kana: ううん。きょうのしあい、ぜんぶまけた。
lines.english: Nah. I lost every match today.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: zenbu? dakara kigen warui n da.
lines.ja: 全部？だから機嫌悪いんだ。
lines.kana: ぜんぶ？だからきげんわるいんだ。
lines.english: Every one? No wonder you're in a mood.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.kana: わるくないよ。なに、そのかお？
lines.english: I'm not in a mood. What's with that face?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nee, kiite! raishuu no nihon to kankoku no shiai, chiketto toreta no!
lines.ja: ねえ、聞いて！来週の日本と韓国の試合、チケット取れたの！
lines.kana: ねえ、きいて！らいしゅうのにほんとかんこくのしあい、ちけっととれたの！
lines.english: Hey, listen! I got tickets for next week's Japan–Korea match!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, uso! sore, chiketto zettai torenai tte, minna itteta yo. dare ni moratta no?
lines.ja: え、うそ！それ、チケット絶対取れないって、みんな言ってたよ。誰にもらったの？
lines.kana: え、うそ！それ、ちけっとぜったいとれないって、みんないってたよ。だれにもらったの？
lines.english: What, no way! Everyone said you'd never get tickets for that. Who gave them to you?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: moratta n ja nai yo. jibun de totta no! juuji kara ichijikan, zutto sumaho mitete.
lines.ja: もらったんじゃないよ。自分で取ったの！10時から1時間、ずっとスマホ見てて。
lines.kana: もらったんじゃないよ。じぶんでとったの！じゅうじからいちじかん、ずっとすまほみてて。
lines.english: Nobody gave them to me. I got them myself! I was glued to my phone for an hour from ten o'clock.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sugoi. ii naa. dare to iku no?
lines.ja: すごい。いいなあ。誰と行くの？
lines.kana: すごい。いいなあ。だれといくの？
lines.english: Wow. Lucky you. Who are you going with?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenji to da yo. ichimai wa kenji no.
lines.ja: ケンジとだよ。一枚はケンジの。
lines.kana: けんじとだよ。いちまいはけんじの。
lines.english: With you! One of them's yours.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: honto ni? yatta! kono mae no shiai wa maketa kedo, kondo wa zettai katsu yo.
lines.ja: ほんとに？やった！この前の試合は負けたけど、今度は絶対勝つよ。
lines.kana: ほんとに？やった！このまえのしあいはまけたけど、こんどはぜったいかつよ。
lines.english: Seriously? Yes! We lost last time, but this time we're definitely winning.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, sou da. sono geemu de mo, nihon to kankoku no shiai, dekiru?
lines.ja: あ、そうだ。そのゲームでも、日本と韓国の試合、できる？
lines.kana: あ、そうだ。そのげーむでも、にほんとかんこくのしあい、できる？
lines.english: Oh, I know. Can you play Japan against Korea in that game too?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: dekiru yo. yatte miru? kekkou muzukashii kedo.
lines.ja: できるよ。やってみる？けっこう難しいけど。
lines.kana: できるよ。やってみる？けっこうむずかしいけど。
lines.english: Yeah. Want to try? It's pretty hard, though.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yatta! katta! kankoku ni katta yo!
lines.ja: やった！勝った！韓国に勝ったよ！
lines.kana: やった！かった！かんこくにかったよ！
lines.english: Yes! I won! I beat Korea!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, hajimete no shiai ni katta no? kotchi wa kyou, zenbu maketa noni.
lines.ja: え、初めての試合に勝ったの？こっちは今日、全部負けたのに。
lines.kana: え、はじめてのしあいにかったの？こっちはきょう、ぜんぶまけたのに。
lines.english: What, you won your very first match? I lost every single one today.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un! kenji ga kono geemu ni hamaru no, wakaru. mou ikkai!
lines.ja: うん！ケンジがこのゲームにハマるの、わかる。もう一回！
lines.kana: うん！けんじがこのげーむにはまるの、わかる。もういっかい！
lines.english: Yep! I totally get why you're hooked on this game. One more!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sakki made monku itteta noni. mou hamatteru jan.
lines.ja: さっきまで文句言ってたのに。もうハマってるじゃん。
lines.kana: さっきまでもんくいってたのに。もうはまってるじゃん。
lines.english: A minute ago you were complaining about it. Now you're hooked yourself.

choices.english: A friend gave Yuki tickets to the Japan–Korea match, and she says Kenji can only come if he stops playing his game.
Yuki got tickets to the Japan–Korea match for herself and Kenji, then tried his game, won, and got hooked on it herself.
Yuki got tickets to the Japan–Korea match, but she won't take Kenji because he lost every match in his game.

questions.explanation: Line 7: Yuki got tickets (chiketto toreta) for next week's Japan–Korea match, and in line 9 she says she got them herself. Line 11: one of the two is Kenji's (ichimai wa kenji no). Lines 13-15: she plays Japan against Korea in his game and wins. Lines 17-18: she wants another go, and Kenji points out she's hooked now (mou hamatteru jan). A is wrong: nobody gave her the tickets (line 9: moratta n ja nai yo), and she never sets a condition. C is wrong: Kenji does lose every match today (line 4), but Yuki is taking him (line 11).

questions.english: Yuki asks what you've been doing at weekends lately. Tell her you're hooked on a game right now, using hamaru.
questions.ja: 最近、週末は何してるの？
questions.kana: さいきん、しゅうまつはなにしてるの？
questions.romaji: saikin, shuumatsu wa nani shiteru no?
questions.answer: Say what you're into right now with ni and hamatteru (am hooked): saikin, geemu ni hamatteru n da. Keep ni, never o. To explain why it eats your weekends, geemu ni hamatchatte (I've got hooked, so...) works well.

modelAnswers.romaji: saikin, sakkaa no geemu ni hamatteru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 最近、サッカーのゲームにハマってるんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Lately I'm hooked on a football game.

modelAnswers.romaji: geemu ni hamatchatte, shuumatsu wa zutto uchi ni iru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ゲームにハマっちゃって、週末はずっとうちにいるよ。
modelAnswers.english: I've got hooked on a game, so I'm home all weekend.

questions.explanation: Kenji says 'saikin, kono geemu ni metcha hamatteru n da' in line 2, and Yuki uses the same pair in line 17 (kono geemu ni hamaru no, wakaru). The game takes ni, not o. 'geemu ga suki' would only say you like games in general; hamatteru says you're into one right now. Yuki is a friend asking casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: Yuki plays her first match in Kenji's game. What does she shout at the end of it?
questions.ja: ユキは、ゲームの試合のあとで、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきは、げーむのしあいのあとで、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki wa, geemu no shiai no ato de, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I beat Korea! (with o, as in English)

questions.explanation: Line 15: 'yatta! katta! kankoku ni katta yo!' The team you beat takes ni, just like the match itself: Kenji answers 'hajimete no shiai ni katta no?' (line 16). A follows English 'beat Korea' with o, but katsu never takes o, and o katta sounds like the past of kau (buy), so it comes out as 'I bought Korea!'. B is the opposite result: maketa means lost, but Yuki shouts yatta! and Kenji can't believe she won her very first match.

questions.english: Yuki asks Kenji if he's any good at his football game, and he says, "kyou no shiai, zenbu maketa." What does he mean?
questions.ja: ケンジは、今日どうでしたか？
questions.kana: けんじは、きょうどうでしたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa, kyou dou deshita ka?

choices.english: He lost every match he played in the game today.
All his saved games got wiped today.
He missed all of today's matches on TV.

questions.explanation: Line 4: makeru is losing a contest, and these are the matches Kenji plays in his football game (Yuki has just asked if he's any good at it, line 3). He says it again in line 16 (kotchi wa kyou, zenbu maketa noni) when Yuki wins her first match. B mixes makeru up with losing a thing, which is nakusu in Japanese, never makeru. C is missing a match, not losing one, and nobody mentions TV.

questions.english: You've got tickets for a sold-out football match. Kenta can't believe it and asks you this. Tell him nobody gave them to you: you got them yourself.
questions.ja: え、あの試合のチケット？誰にもらったの？
questions.kana: え、あのしあいのちけっと？だれにもらったの？
questions.romaji: e, ano shiai no chiketto? dare ni moratta no?
questions.answer: Say you got them yourself with toru: jibun de totta (or yatto toreta, finally managed to get them). moratta is what Kenta is asking about (someone gave them to you), so you can set the two against each other: moratta n ja nai yo, jibun de totta n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: moratta n ja nai yo. jibun de totta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: もらったんじゃないよ。自分で取ったんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Nobody gave them to me. I got them myself.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, jibun de totta yo. ichijikan kakatta kedo, yatto toreta.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、自分で取ったよ。1時間かかったけど、やっと取れた。
modelAnswers.english: No, I got them myself. It took an hour, but I finally got them.

questions.explanation: In line 9 Yuki answers Kenji's 'dare ni moratta no?' the same way: 'moratta n ja nai yo. jibun de totta no!' Tickets you get hold of yourself are chiketto o toru, and 'I got them!' is toreta (line 7: chiketto toreta no!; line 8: chiketto zettai torenai, there's no way to get any). moratta means someone gave them to you, which is exactly what you're denying. katta (bought) isn't wrong, but it doesn't say you managed to get hold of them. Kenta is a friend, so answer casually.
